Today's verdict BEARISH-DEFENSIVE
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index 1/10: only 1-2 price-based signals firing, minimal realized stress vs VIX Spike Tier 4/4: EXTREME, 85% probability of vol expansion, backwardation and skew both active
These measure different things. The Crash Index reads spot price behavior; the VIX Spike reads what options traders are paying for forward protection. They can coexist when price is calm but the options market is pricing a move that has not happened yet. Trust the Tier 4 read as the leading signal until price confirms otherwise.
Today's tension
Crash Index at **1/10** while the VIX Spike Detector sits at its maximum tier: the options market is pricing extreme fear that spot prices have not confirmed.
Bull
The Crash Index sits at **1/10** with no active confluences, meaning price-based stress signals are not firing. The contrarian score at **46** says partial accumulation conditions exist, and the extreme options positioning could itself become fuel for a squeeze if the vol expansion fails to materialize.
Bear
The VIX Spike Detector is at Tier **4/4** with backwardation, skew, and adaptive all active, pricing an **85%** probability of vol expansion. The divergence composite is in a TOPPING zone with **26** bearish cross-asset pairs against only **4** bullish pairs across **43** total relationships.
The tell: Whether any of the three confluence pairs activate, particularly T1 paired with HYG. That combination of VIX backwardation with credit stress is the read that separates options-market noise from genuine macro deterioration.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The macro tape today is defined by one central split: spot prices are quiet enough that the Crash Index registers only 1 out of 10, but the options market is at its maximum fear tier, pricing an 85% probability of a vol expansion with backwardation, skew, and adaptive signals all live. The macro regime sits at CONCENTRATION with 55% confidence, and the regime state score of 47 puts the market in TRANSITION with mixed bias. Breadth is fracturing underneath: 26 cross-asset pairs are diverging bearishly versus 4 bullishly, with 69.8% of all 43 tracked pairs now decoupled from their prior correlations.

For positioning, CONCENTRATION means the leaders are doing the work and the rest are not. NDX is up +3.3% over five days while RUT is down -0.8%. You stay in the concentrated winners and reduce exposure to the laggards. The contrarian score at 46 gives you a partial accumulate signal, meaning conditions are tilting toward opportunity but have not fully resolved. You add selectively, not broadly.

The read that flips this stance is a confirmed activation of any confluence pair, especially T1 paired with HYG. Credit joining the vol stress would shift the calculus from selective accumulation toward defensiveness. All three confluences are inactive right now, which keeps the bear case in the options surface rather than in fundamentals.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The macro regime is CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence. CONCENTRATION means return dispersion is elevated: a small group of assets is generating the gains while the rest underperform or go sideways.

NDX +3.3% against RUT -0.8% over five days is the US version. KOSPI +5.4% against ASX -0.3% is the Asia version.

SOL +9.8% against ETH +1.9% is the crypto version. The regime state score of 47 places the market in TRANSITION with mixed bias, which means the CONCENTRATION read has not locked in.

It could resolve into broader participation or fracture into defensiveness. At 55% confidence, you size for the regime but keep capacity for the resolution.

The contrarian score at 46 (partial ACCUMULATE) is consistent with that read.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

The divergence composite is in a TOPPING zone with 69.8% of the 43 tracked pairs moving apart from their historical correlations, 26 of those in a bearish direction against only 4 bullish. Divergence means correlation breakdown: two assets that normally move together stop doing so.

When that happens across most of your cross-asset map, stress is building under the surface before price confirms it. The mother jaws score is at its ceiling of 100.

The sharpest breaks are in QQQ versus SPY, where the correlation drifted from +0.81 to -0.31 (the Nasdaq and the S&P are no longer moving in lockstep), and in KRE versus XLF, where regional banks broke away from the broader financials index (from +0.18 to -0.66). USMV versus SPY flipped from -0.92 to +0.04, meaning the low-volatility defensive factor is no longer moving inversely to the index the way it historically has.

That is a structural shift in factor behavior. GDX versus GLD moved from +0.19 to +0.75, with miners pulling tighter to gold itself, suggesting capital is treating them as a purer commodity proxy rather than as equity.

AI read · what the confluences mean now

All three confluence pairs are inactive today. VIX backwardation is live at Tier 4/4, but it has not combined with credit stress in HYG, small-cap drawdown in B2, or yen safe-haven flows to trigger a confirmed cascade signal.

That absence matters. When backwardation occurs without credit or currency confirmation, it reflects options-driven hedging rather than fundamental deterioration.

Watch HYG specifically. If credit spreads start moving in tandem with the options stress, the first confluence activates and the positioning calculus shifts from selective accumulation toward outright defensiveness.

The Tier 4 vol read is a warning, not a confirmed signal, until at least one pairing fires.

The five-day cross-region tape has one consistent theme: growth and tech are being bought; everything else is being left behind. KOSPI leads all regions at +5.4% while ASX drags at -0.3% in Asia.

SOL +9.8% against ETH +1.9% in crypto repeats the same structure at higher beta. All four regions are showing the same behavior: capital concentrates into the highest-conviction growth proxies and withdraws from the broad market, which is the strongest possible confirmation of the CONCENTRATION macro regime read.

Forward-looking indicators · Bonferroni-validated
Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 1/10 and the VIX Spike Detector at Tier 4/4 are reading two different markets. The Crash Index measures spot price behavior: how many price-level stress signals are active today.

The VIX Spike reads the options surface: near-term vol is more expensive than out months (backwardation is active), puts carry an unusual premium over calls (skew is active), and the adaptive threshold is breached. The options market is paying up to hedge a move that spot prices have not confirmed.

That gap between implied and realized stress is itself the signal. It closes one of two ways: price breaks and the Crash Index catches up, or the vol bid fades and the Tier 4 reading comes down.

At 85% probability of a vol expansion and zero active confluence pairs, you are in the window where the options market could be right before price confirms it.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
